title: Consolidation
objective: Give each cross-cutting mechanism one implementation that every feature extends, fix the defects where copies diverged, and delete the copies, with no product change beyond the owner's 2026-09-24 decisions.
context_summary: The whole-codebase review of 2026-09-24 found most cross-cutting mechanisms implemented two or more times by parallel feature work, with confirmed defects where copies disagree. The design lists each concept, its copies and its replacement, and the owner's decisions are recorded. Wave 1 fixes defects and deletes; later waves consolidate the core, the module contract, the desktop, rendering and the harness.

tasks.description: Make a deduplicated retry emit no event, refuse an unrouted method explicitly, give Restore the same admission checks as every commit, and plan each preset step against its own target so presets work on masked photos.
extra_context: A deduplicated mutation result keeps `outcome: applied`, and the owner's event check reads only the outcome, so a retried request records a second event.
A method with no service handler that no owner layer matches falls through to the `events.since` answer; it must fail as an internal error naming the method.

`EditorService::restore` runs only registry recipe validation, while `commit_snapshot` also validates the source recipe, records and requires artifacts and compiles. One admission function serves both, and no copy of the checks stays behind.

A preset's `Compose` steps plan against the whole resolved recipe, while a direct action plans against `recipe_for_target`. With a global and a masked Basic layer a preset is refused as ambiguous; with only a masked one it silently edits the masked layer. `capture_preset` reads layers the same way.

acceptance_criteria: A retried mutation that is answered from the request table records no event; the first attempt still records one.

Restore and every other commit admit a recipe through one function, and Restore refuses what a commit refuses (for example a stack naming a missing stroke).

Applying and capturing a preset on a stack with a global and a masked Basic layer uses the global layer, and on a stack with only a masked Basic layer creates or reads a global one; the masked layer is untouched.

steps: Add a test per acceptance criterion beside the code it covers.
Run the existing history, deduplication, restore, preset and mask command tests.
expected_results: The new tests fail before the change and pass after it; existing tests pass unchanged.

tasks.description: Send a mask gesture's `draft.set` synchronously on the desktop thread, as the slider gesture does, and stop a late answer from presenting a drafted frame after Discard.
extra_context: The slider calls `tasks::draft_set_now` synchronously because a runtime hop costs one display frame during a drag (performance rule 12). The mask gesture sends the same request through `Task::perform` in `mask_draft_set_task`, and the measured paint latency misses its bound.

`mask_cancel` sends `draft.cancel` while a `draft.set` may be in flight, and the `MaskDraftSet` handler stores the draft and requests its preview without checking that the gesture still exists. The slider defers its cancel until the in-flight answer arrives.
The single desktop draft driver comes in wave 4; this task changes only the hop and the race, reusing `draft_set_now`.
A comment in `app/masks.rs` still calls the overlay for a pixel-reading mask (P16) open; it is built.

tasks.description: Key a spatial unit's global estimate by what its preparation reads, reduce the stage only when a missing unit needs an estimate, describe units without rounding, decide proxy approximation from the compiled operations, and take test-only counters and estimate hooks out of the public API.
extra_context: `resolve_globals` keys each unit by its `describe()` string, which includes the amount, so every new Presence value misses and reduces the whole stage on both preview phases. Clarity and Texture prepare no estimate yet still trigger the reduction; Dehaze's estimate does not depend on its amount.
Unit `describe()` strings round their values although they are used as identities (operation equality and the estimate key).
`proxy_approximate` decides by effect stage, so a reset Presence layer, which compiles to nothing, labels exact proxy frames approximate.

`masked_tile_counts`, `reset_masked_tile_counts`, `cached_estimates` and `clear_estimates` are exported from `lib.rs` and used only by tests; the masked-tile counters are process-global atomics bumped on the hot path.

tasks.description: Keep at most two spatial frames alive on the RAW path, stop copying every finished frame into a new allocation, allocate colour scratch once per worker, delete render code only tests use, and correct the RAW Planckian coefficient.
extra_context: `LinearEvaluation` keeps every spatial segment's full float frame for the whole evaluation, up to five at 60 MP, against the architecture's two-frame rule.

Renders end by converting `Vec<u8>` into `Arc<[u8]>`, which allocates and copies the whole frame; the linear and proxy paths do the same. The colour pass allocates a fresh scratch buffer per row chunk.
`render::locate`, `Evaluation::locate`, `locate_in` and `ProxyCache::is_empty` are used only by tests; production uses `locate_dimensions`.
The RAW white-balance locus uses 0.2343580e6 where the published Kim et al. coefficient, the Basic copy, its reference and the design use 0.2343589e6. The shared colour module arrives in wave 3.

tasks.description: Bound a point query through more than one spatial segment: each spatial tile is evaluated at most once per query, through one tile cache shared by the byte and RAW point paths, so a sample equals the rendered byte at a bounded cost.
extra_context: On the byte path a point sample through two spatial segments runs a whole inner tile for every pixel of the outer tile and for every pixel the global reduction reads, with no caching; measured in release, a centre sample on a 48×36 image goes from 0.1 ms with one spatial layer to 187 ms with two, and at the real 512 px tile it is effectively a hang. A global plus a masked Presence layer on a JPEG reaches it through `render.sample`, grid samples and the layer-input overlay, all on the catalog owner.

The RAW point path keeps up to four evaluated tiles for the rest of a request so a resample's four neighbours evaluate each tile once; the byte path has no such cache, so a sample through Presence and a straightened crop also runs the tile chain four or five times.
The fix is one cache for both paths, bounded by the spatial budget, not a second mechanism.

acceptance_criteria: Each spatial segment's tile is evaluated at most once per point query on both paths, proved by counting tile evaluations in tests with two and three spatial segments and under a straightened crop.
A sample equals the rendered byte on both paths for those stacks.
One cache serves both paths.
The design and performance rules state the bounded cost of a point query through several spatial segments.

expected_results: Counts are bounded as stated; exactness tests pass unchanged.

tasks.description: Route every host method through one table whose entries are service or owner handlers, declare each method's parameters once so the schema and the parser cannot differ, and give every mutating method the same `{request_id, actor}` envelope with deduplication.
extra_context: Today 31 handler-less methods are routed by three string-match layers in the owner loop plus the capability host's own match, and the event append is copied three times beside `record_event`.

Parameters are declared as required and optional strings in `METHODS`, again as about 37 serde structs, and again in a hand-copied schema test; the parser exists four times and clones the request; five methods ignore their parameters, against the rule that a misspelt filter is never silently ignored.

The owner decided on 2026-09-24 that every mutating method carries `{request_id, actor}` and is deduplicated, with `expected_revision` wherever a revision exists; today presets, versions, resources and artifacts use four different conventions.
acceptance_criteria: One table dispatches every host method; the owner loop has no per-method string match and no fallthrough.
Each method's parameters are declared once and generate both the schema and the parser; every method refuses an unknown parameter.
Every mutating method takes `{request_id, actor}` and a retry returns the first answer; the desktop, `lightwell-json`, xtask and the docs use the new shapes.
The event recording, held-draft lookup and selected-entry resolution each exist once.

steps: A generated test sends every listed method its declared fields and gets no unknown-field error, and one unknown field gets a validation error.
A retry test per mutating method family.
expected_results: All pass; schema.list matches the parsers by construction.

tasks.description: Cache the catalog owner's immutable history entries with their strokes resolved, share a recipe's stroke table instead of deep-copying it, give drafts a revision read that decodes nothing, and store the RAW interpretation typed instead of re-parsing JSON on every read.
extra_context: Every `state()` and `entry()` decodes the entry's JSON and hydrates its strokes (a SQL lookup, a SHA-256 and a parse per referenced stroke); one slider tick reads the state three times, one only to compare the revision, and `render.sample` three times.

Entries are immutable, enforced by the catalog's trigger, and the owner is the only writer over an exclusive connection, so a small cache of entries keyed by entry id and a head per asset updated by every write is coherent by construction.
`StrokeTable` derives a deep `Clone` over a map of point vectors, so every recipe clone copies every stroke; it is immutable after hydration.
`SourceKind::Raw { metadata: Value }` is re-parsed on every state read and in every source-recipe validation, and compared through a JSON round trip to work around f32/f64 inequality.
acceptance_criteria: A state or entry read after the first costs no JSON decode or stroke hash, proved by a test that counts them; every write keeps the cache coherent, proved by tests over commit, undo, redo, restore, import and reopen.
Cloning a recipe does not copy its strokes.
A draft's conflict check reads the revision without decoding an entry.
The RAW interpretation is typed and parsed once per asset row.

steps: Counting tests for decodes and hashes; coherence tests per write path; the existing history, mask and RAW tests.
expected_results: All pass; reads after the first decode nothing.

tasks.description: Give every catalog write one path: a `mutate` that validates the envelope, answers a retry, checks the revision, runs the caller's plan, admits the recipe once and writes one transaction that also updates the entry cache; one `write` helper and `From<rusqlite::Error>` for every transaction, including the preset library and the artifact store.
extra_context: Write transactions are hand-built for import, commit, navigate, restore, version create and delete and persisted no-ops; `HistoryEntry` and `MutationResult` literals and the redo-clearing SQL are copied; one commit validates its recipe several times, including again inside `insert_entry`'s transaction.

Restore's transaction has no request-absent check, so a concurrent duplicate is a catalog error rather than a conflict; `commit_snapshot` assigns `state.current_entry` to a value it then drops; a doc comment meant for `insert_entry` sits on `default_artifact_root`.
About 95 `.map_err(catalog_error)` and 13 `transaction_with_behavior` blocks repeat across the editor, the preset library and the artifact store.
The entry cache updates after each committed write; with one write path it updates in one place.
acceptance_criteria: Commit, undo, redo, restore, versions and no-ops go through one `mutate`; import and the preset library and artifact store use the one `write` helper; the copied literals and SQL exist once.

tasks.description: Carry a recipe's prepared artifacts on the recipe, as its strokes are, so compiling reads them from the recipe instead of a process-global weak index kept alive by pins that every caller must remember.

Forgetting one is a runtime `artifact … is not prepared` error.
Strokes already solve the same problem: `Recipe.strokes` is `#[serde(skip)]`, filled when an entry is read, excluded from equality, and compilation refuses its recorded faults.
A binding step that finds an artifact not prepared still answers `preparation-required` exactly as today.

extra_context: The desktop parses evidence scripts by hand in `app/evidence.rs` and xtask writes them by hand; one crate of serde-derived types serves both.
acceptance_criteria: One crate defines the evidence script types, used by the desktop and xtask; the hand parsers and writers are deleted.
Every smoke scenario still runs, and a deliberately broken step fails as before.

steps: App and xtask tests; rendered tier.

tasks.description: Build test support on `lightwell-testkit` and an independent `lightwell-reference` crate that cannot depend on the core, with fewer test binaries, the per-module field-patch tests in the field-patch suite, the historical-parity tests deleted and xtask's acceptance JSON helpers on the conformance client.
extra_context: Test helpers are copied per test binary; the core has one integration-test binary per file (mask tests alone are about a dozen).
Reference implementations live in the core's test tree and can import the code they check; a `lightwell-reference` crate that cannot depend on `lightwell-core` makes them independent by construction.
Per-module field-patch tests remain in `basic`, `mixer`, `presence` and `vignette` beside the shared field-patch conformance suite.
`tests/basic_tone.rs` and `tests/basic_colour.rs` compare against values saved before an earlier change, which the current-shapes rule forbids.
xtask's `basic_acceptance.rs` has its own JSON helpers beside the conformance suite's client.

context_links.label: Core tests
context_links.relevance: One of the mask test binaries.

acceptance_criteria: `lightwell-testkit` holds the shared helpers and `lightwell-reference` holds the independent references with no dependency on the core; the copies are deleted.
The mask tests are one binary and the core has fewer test binaries.
Per-module field-patch tests live in the field-patch suite.
The historical-parity tests are deleted.
xtask's acceptance uses the conformance client.
Every remaining check still runs and passes.

steps: Core and xtask tests; quick tier.

tasks.description: Replace the private error helper copies with error constructors such as `Error::validation(..)`, last, because it touches everything.
extra_context: Modules and services build errors with `Error::new(ErrorKind::X, ..)` and private helper copies; constructors per kind replace them.
acceptance_criteria: Every private error helper copy is replaced by a constructor; error codes and messages are unchanged.
The quick tier passes.

steps: Core and app tests.

tasks.description: Correct the documentation the review found stale: the modules-and-API design's Basic and effects rows, Basic's field descriptions of its input, the instant-preview restatement of the slider budget, and architecture's Persistence paragraph.
extra_context: `docs/design/modules-and-api.md` says Basic implements only `exposure`, and its effects row omits `maskable`.
Basic's field descriptions call the input "a rendered sRGB JPEG" although RAW feeds it linear data.
`docs/design/instant-preview.md` restates the slider budget that the performance spec owns.
`docs/design/architecture.md`'s Persistence paragraph has grown long; it is trimmed to current behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: Each item reads as current behaviour; descriptor text changes are reflected in `schema.list`.
The repository check passes.
